A shared view of your data

For traffic engineers, transportation agencies, researchers, and consultants who need to understand how conditions change across space and time.

Where TrafficCube fits

A practical bridge from traffic data to analysis.

TrafficCube complements established traffic modeling tools, large commercial online analytics platforms, and agency-hosted data environments.

Those larger platforms can provide integrated data feeds, enterprise workflows, and ongoing network management. TrafficCube offers a lightweight desktop environment for focused studies: organizing multisource data, inspecting patterns, and applying repeatable analytical methods across locations, time intervals, days, and simulation runs.

Its niche is to make spatiotemporal analysis more accessible to agencies, consultants, and researchers, while providing a practical setting to examine and test methods that could later be incorporated into larger systems.

Planning

Understand conditions.
Define the study.

Data analytics tools like TrafficCube can help analysts understand traffic network conditions and define spatiotemporal analysis limits: the roadway extent, times of day, and operating conditions that a study should capture.

Design

Check models.
Strengthen confidence.

Use structured observed and simulated data to support verification, calibration, and validation (VC&V) of traffic modeling tools. Examine where model results agree with field conditions and where further investigation or adjustment is needed.

Operations & maintenance

Evaluate changes.
Track performance.

Data analytics can support before-and-after analysis of transportation investments and system monitoring over time. Compare similar operating conditions, examine localized effects, and identify changes that warrant closer attention.

These roles describe the broader value of data analytics across the project lifecycle. TrafficCube’s available functions and planned developments are described separately below; automated real-time monitoring is a future application.

From observations to understanding

Follow congestion across locations and time.

Examine speed and travel-time patterns alongside potential contributing conditions. Look for upstream effects and congestion that persists into later intervals.

Start with the included two-week demonstration data, then explore optional full-year datasets. The synthetic examples provide a controlled environment for learning the workflow.

Get started

Open the demo. Explore your own data.

The application runs on your Windows computer. GitHub hosts the software downloads, sample datasets, and release instructions.

01 / DOWNLOAD

Get the application

Open the software release page and download TrafficCube.zip. Check the release instructions for installation details.

02 / EXTRACT & RUN

Launch TrafficCube

Before extracting, right-click the ZIP and choose Properties → Unblock, if shown. Extract it and run TrafficCube.Desktop.exe.

03 / EXPLORE

Load the sample CSVs

Choose Open in TrafficCube and select one or several demo files. Use the examples to prepare your own CSV datasets.
